metaDescription: Odoo Sign in practice: Enterprise only, no per envelope charge, what the audit trail actually proves, and where a qualified signature is still required.
intro: Odoo Sign turns a finished PDF into a signing workflow. You upload the document once, drag signature, text, date and checkbox fields onto it, assign each field to a role such as employer or tenant, then send. Each signer gets a private link, fills only their own fields in the browser, and signs by drawing, typing or uploading an image. Nobody outside the company needs an Odoo login to complete a document.

The licence position decides most evaluations. Sign is an Enterprise app and there is no Community equivalent, although the accept and sign step on a portal quotation belongs to Sales and works without it. Enterprise does not meter signature requests, so there is no per envelope charge. That is the usual reason a company already holding a subscription stops renewing a separate signature vendor.

What Odoo produces is an ordinary electronic signature supported by an event log: who opened the link, from which IP address, at what time, and the completed file stored against the request. It is not a qualified electronic signature, and Odoo is not a licensed trust service provider. For most commercial paperwork that distinction never surfaces. For the small set of documents where a statute prescribes written form, it decides the project.
whoFor: Companies with a steady flow of standard paperwork: non disclosure agreements, service agreements, supplier terms, delivery acceptance and policy sign offs.
HR teams issuing offer letters, contracts, probation confirmations and handbook acknowledgements to people who will never be Odoo users.
Businesses already paying for Odoo Enterprise per user while also paying an envelope based signature vendor for the same documents.
Rental, leasing and subscription operators sending the same agreement hundreds of times with three fields changing.
Not for documents where the law demands a qualified electronic signature or a witnessed wet signature, such as a German notice of termination or an English deed.
Not for document assembly either, because Sign places fields on a finished PDF and does nothing about the clauses inside it.

capabilities.title: Templates, roles and the field set
capabilities.body: A template is a PDF plus the fields placed on it. Field types cover signature, initial, single line and multiline text, checkbox, selection, date, name, email, phone and company. Every field belongs to a role, which is what lets one lease template serve landlord and tenant without maintaining two documents. Fields can be required or optional. Placement is stored as a position on a page, so a template is bound to that exact file.

capabilities.title: Fields that fill themselves from the contact
capabilities.body: A field type can be tied to a partner field, so name, email, phone and company arrive prefilled from the record the request was raised against. That removes the most common source of bad contract data, a signer typing their own company name three different ways across three documents. Configure it before the first large send, because retrofitting means reopening every template.

capabilities.title: Sending, order, reminders and expiry
capabilities.body: Sending a template creates one request per signer, each with its own link and its own copy of the document. You can set a reminder in days, a validity date after which the request expires, and on recent versions a signing order so the second party is invited only once the first has signed. The list of outstanding requests is the part managers actually use every day.

capabilities.title: Authentication beyond the emailed link
capabilities.body: By default, assurance rests on possession of a link sent to a named address. That is proportionate for an internal policy acknowledgement and thin for a six figure contract. An extra verification step by SMS can be enabled per role, sending a code the signer enters before signing. SMS runs on Odoo IAP credits bought separately, so it carries a real per message cost and belongs on high value templates only.

capabilities.title: The audit trail and the finished file
capabilities.body: Each request keeps a log of the events behind it, including the IP address, the timestamp and the address the link was sent to. When the last party signs, the field values are flattened into the PDF, the file is stored on the request, and a copy goes to everyone involved. In a dispute it is the log and the stored file together that carry weight, not the picture of the signature.

capabilities.title: Share links for documents everyone signs
capabilities.body: A template can be published as a shareable link instead of being sent to named people. Anyone opening it generates a fresh request and signs their own copy, which suits waivers, site induction forms and annual policy acknowledgements. The trade off is identity: a share link proves somebody typed a name, so pair it with an internal check when the document has to be tied to a specific person.

setup.title: Inventory the documents before building anything
setup.body: Start with a list of every recurring document, who signs it, in what order, and whether any statute constrains it. Most mid sized companies find around twenty, of which five or six templates carry the large majority of volume. The list is where legal review happens once rather than per document, and where the two or three that must stay on paper get identified early.

setup.title: Author the PDF upstream and freeze it
setup.body: Sign does not write documents. The PDF comes from Word, from an Odoo report, or from whatever the legal team already uses, and Sign only decorates it. Keep the source file under version control with a visible version number in the footer. When a clause changes and the text reflows, every field below the edit moves, so a revised PDF is a new template rather than an edit.

setup.title: Roles, access levels and who may send
setup.body: Roles are defined once and reused across templates, so a role list mirroring how the business names parties saves rework later. The app also has its own access levels separating people who build templates from people who only send existing ones. Give template authoring to two or three named users. Everyone else sends. That single decision prevents a library of forty near identical drafts.

setup.title: Email delivery is the whole mechanism
setup.body: A signature request is an email carrying a link, so contracts arrive only if the sending domain passes SPF, DKIM and DMARC. Configure the outgoing mail server and the bounce address properly, then test into a Gmail account, a Microsoft 365 tenant and a corporate mail filter before go live. Requests landing in spam look like signers ignoring you, and get diagnosed far too late.

setup.title: Decide where signed files live and for how long
setup.body: Completed PDFs stay on the request and, where the Documents app is in use, can be filed into a workspace with an owner and a folder structure. Nothing deletes anything on its own. Signed contracts hold personal data, so agree a retention period per document type up front, and record who is allowed to open the folder, which matters most for HR paperwork sitting beside ordinary sales agreements.

pitfalls.title: Confusing the Sign app with the quotation signature
pitfalls.body: Odoo has two unrelated signing mechanisms. The Sales portal lets a customer accept and sign a quotation, storing a signature image and a name against the order. The Sign app runs templates, roles and an audit trail. A requirement written as electronic signature gets delivered as whichever one the implementer assumed. Name the one you mean, because the evidence they produce is not equivalent.

pitfalls.title: Templates that quietly break when the wording changes
pitfalls.body: Field positions are coordinates on a page. Insert a paragraph on page two and every field after it sits over the wrong line, which nobody notices until a signer reports that the date box covers a clause. Treat template updates as a controlled change: new PDF, new template, retire the old one, and read the last page before the first live send.

pitfalls.title: Treating the link as proof of identity
pitfalls.body: The person who signs is whoever opened the email. Shared inboxes, forwarded messages and assistants managing a director's mail all break that assumption silently. For anything material, send to a personal address rather than a generic company one, enable SMS verification on that role, and keep a record of how the signer's address was established in the first place. Authority to sign is a separate question again.

pitfalls.title: Signing something the law will not accept electronically
pitfalls.body: Terminations of employment in Germany, deeds in England, wills and property transfers in India, and several court and land registry filings across the Gulf still need ink or a qualified certificate. This is a one time legal review per country, not a judgement made per document by whoever is sending, and it belongs in the first week rather than in the first dispute.

pitfalls.title: No archive, no retention, no backup thinking
pitfalls.body: Signed PDFs accumulate as attachments in the Odoo filestore, which grows quietly until a database backup takes an hour. They also hold personal data that a subject access request or a data protection audit will ask about. Agree a retention rule, confirm the filestore is inside the backup set, and test that a contract signed three years ago can still be found.

worksWith: Documents, for filing completed PDFs into a workspace with an owner and a retention rule
Employees and Recruitment, so an offer can be signed before an employee record exists
Sales, Subscriptions and Rental, for the agreement sitting behind the order rather than the order itself
Contacts, since roles resolve to partners and prefilled fields read from them
The outgoing mail server, because a request is only as reliable as its delivery
Odoo IAP credits, which fund the optional SMS verification step
Studio and automation rules, when a completed signature should move a record forward without a human

regional.note: Employment contracts are authenticated on Qiwa, so the copy Odoo holds is the internal record and the platform version is the one the Ministry recognises. Keep the two identical. ZATCA Phase 2 also relies on a cryptographic stamp issued to the invoicing solution, which is a different mechanism entirely and cannot be produced by Sign. Arabic templates need the PDF laid out right to left before any field is placed.

Federal Decree-Law No. 46 of 2021 on electronic transactions and trust services gives electronic signatures legal effect and defines a higher tier tied to licensed providers. Employment terms still have to match the offer and contract filed with MOHRE, so treat the signed Odoo file as the company record rather than the regulatory one. DIFC and ADGM entities run their own contract rules.

The Electronic Transactions Ordinance 2002 gives electronic documents and signatures legal effect, and the Electronic Certification Accreditation Council accredits the providers whose certificates carry higher evidential weight. Odoo Sign sits below that tier, which is normally sufficient for commercial paperwork and employment letters. Instruments attracting provincial stamp duty, land records and court filings stay on paper.

The Information Technology Act 2000 recognises two routes to a statutory electronic signature: a digital signature certificate from a licensed certifying authority, or Aadhaar based eSign through a licensed provider. Odoo Sign is neither, so it stands as evidence of agreement rather than a statutory signature. Schedule I excludes wills, powers of attorney and property conveyances, and stamp duty remains a separate state obligation.

Law 5070 recognises the guvenli elektronik imza, a qualified signature carried on a certificate from a licensed ESHS provider, and only that form substitutes for a wet signature where writing is required. Formal notices are normally served through KEP registered electronic mail. Templates need Turkish text and Turkish date order, because a document produced only in English gets argued about later.

Electronic signatures sit under Law 15 of 2004, with ITIDA licensing the certification service providers that issue them. The signature the ETA e-invoicing system demands is one of those, held on a token or an HSM and applied by the invoicing solution, so it is a separate mechanism from Sign. Arabic contract text and Egyptian pound amounts belong in the PDF before fields go on.

Where a statute prescribes Schriftform, section 126a BGB permits an electronic substitute only with a qualified electronic signature, which Odoo does not issue. Notice of termination under section 623 BGB rules out electronic form altogether and still needs ink. Ordinary commercial agreements are fine. Signed PDFs also fall under GoBD, so they must be stored unaltered and stay readable for the retention period.

Simple electronic signatures are valid for most contracts, confirmed by the Electronic Communications Act 2000 and the Law Commission review in 2019. Deeds are the exception: they need a witness physically present when the signatory signs, and Sign has no witness role, so those go back to paper or to a specialist provider. Retention of signed personal data falls under UK GDPR.

faqs.q: Is Odoo Sign available in Community?
faqs.a: No. Sign is an Enterprise app and Community has no equivalent with templates, roles and an audit trail. Community can still store a signed PDF as an attachment, and the accept and sign step on a portal quotation belongs to Sales rather than Sign, so that particular flow does work without Enterprise. Everything else needs it.

faqs.q: Do the people signing need an Odoo user licence?
faqs.a: No. External signers open a link, complete their fields and never log in, so they cost nothing. Only the staff who build templates and send requests consume a user licence. That is why the cost curve stays flat as signing volume grows, which is the opposite of envelope based pricing.

faqs.q: Is there a charge per document or per envelope?
faqs.a: Odoo does not meter signature requests, so volume does not change the subscription. The only usage cost is the optional SMS verification step, which consumes Odoo IAP credits bought in advance. Budget those separately, and enable SMS only on the templates where the extra assurance is worth the per message price.

faqs.q: Is a signature made in Odoo legally binding?
faqs.a: In most of the countries covered here an electronic signature is admissible and enforceable for ordinary commercial agreements, and the event log Odoo keeps is the evidence behind it. What Odoo does not produce is a qualified electronic signature backed by a certificate from a licensed trust service provider, which specific document types and specific countries require.

faqs.q: Can we change a contract after the template is built?
faqs.a: Yes, with a routine. Fields are anchored to positions on the page, so text that reflows leaves them misaligned. Upload the revised PDF as a new template, place the fields again, send a test to yourself, then archive the previous version so nobody accidentally sends last year's terms to a customer.

faqs.q: Can we send the same document to two hundred people at once?
faqs.a: Yes. Selecting a template and a list of recipients creates one request per person, each with its own link and its own signed copy, so the audit trail stays per signer. Where everyone signs the same document without being individually invited, a share link is simpler and still produces a record per person.

faqs.q: Can Odoo Sign replace a dedicated signature vendor completely?
faqs.a: For internal paperwork and standard commercial agreements, usually yes, and the saving is real for a company already on Enterprise. It does not cover qualified signatures, remote online notarisation, or identity verified signing in regulated flows such as lending. Those stay with a specialist provider, and they are a small share of most document volumes.
